properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js (SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations, elliptic's hashing dependency) ships in the lesson-4 toolchain image; no application call site. The SHA-2 family is Grover-square-root only — not urgent; SHA-1 within it is legacy.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is the Ethereum transaction-signing curve, fixed by the blockchain protocol — not changeable inside this repo, but the project's own scripts (ethers.getSigners() → deploy()/fund() in lesson-4/5/6 scripts and tasks) exercise it for every signed transaction. This object records availability via the dependency tree; the use site is reported separately as a finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenSSL's legacy single-round MD5-based KDF, used by the browserify cipher stack to turn passwords into cipher keys. It ships with the toolchain the project builds with; no application call site found — presence-only asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.3.0 declared in lesson-4's package-lock.json ships secp256k1 ECDSA — the curve every Ethereum wallet/signer uses for transaction and message signing. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor; migration is ecosystem-level (no PQ signature scheme is standardized in the EVM yet), so changeable here only by following the Ethereum roadmap. Same package as LIB-e9aa10c7 (library object) and ALG-a6da3577 (P-256 capability).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Quantum-vulnerable signature implementation present in the shipped dependency tree; no application call site in lesson-4's code. Availability is what this inventory records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic ships ECDSA over secp256k1/P-256 curves in the toolchain's dependency tree; no direct call site in lesson-4 application code (the toolchain uses it indirectly via ethereumjs).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves@1.3.0 also provides P-256/secp256r1 ECDSA+ECDH; declared in lesson-4's lockfile. No first-party call site in the lesson code — presence is what the inventory records (reachable through the Ethereum JS toolchain that depends on it).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 (declared in lesson-4's lockfile) ships ECDH key agreement on secp256k1/secp256r1 plus ECDSA — pulled in transitively by the Ethereum JS toolchain. Quantum-vulnerable key agreement (harvest-now-decrypt-later class); replaceable by moving deps to ML-KEM-based stacks when the ecosystem offers them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Quantum-vulnerable key-agreement implementation available in the shipped dependency tree; no application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 dependency inventory: all 53 sites are manifest entries (@ethersproject/keccak256, keccak@3.0.2, @noble/hashes sha3) across the lesson-4/5/6 lockfiles. Keccak-256 is the EVM workhorse hash (transaction digests, EIP-712 typed-data hashing, event topics, address derivation). Hashes retain preimage security under Grover — not a PQ migration priority, but it is the cryptographic spine of everything these lessons deploy, so it belongs in the inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 is the password KDF ethers uses for wallet/keystore files. Pulled in by the hardhat toolchain; the project itself derives no keys from passwords in the code on disk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-js@3.0.1/^3.0.0 manifest entries in all three lockfiles — the password-based KDF the Ethereum JS toolchain uses for keystore-v3 (BIP-32/EIP-2335-style) wallet file encryption. Parameters (N, r, p) are chosen at runtime by the keystore code, not pinned in the manifest.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is available via ethers v6's hashing module; hashes only weaken by Grover's square root, so not urgent for migration. No application call site in lesson code; presence-only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 implementation available via @noble/hashes in the shipped dependency tree; no application call site. Hash, not Shor-vulnerable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: SHA-3/Keccak capability of @noble/hashes@1.3.3, declared in lesson-4's lockfile. Same package as LIB-b3a1e7cf (the library-level object) — kept separate so the SHA-3 algorithm record survives alongside the library record.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Classical AEAD (Salsa20 stream cipher + Poly1305 MAC) available in the dependency tree; not Shor-broken but a legacy primitive; no application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@1.0.3 (plus tweetnacl-util) declared in the lesson-4 and lesson-6 lockfiles as a transitive dependency of the Ethereum JS toolchain. TweetNaCl ships Ed25519 signatures, X25519 key agreement, XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE and SHA-512 — all quantum-vulnerable primitives bundled with what these lessons build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes (versions 1.3.2/1.3.3/1.4.0 across the lesson-4 and lesson-6 lockfiles) — the hash/KDF library of the modern Ethereum stack (viem/@scure/ethereum-cryptography v2), shipping SHA-2, SHA-3/Keccak, BLAKE2/3, HKDF, PBKDF2, scrypt. No direct first-party call site found in the lesson code; the shipped manifest is the asset.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/curves (versions 1.2.0/1.3.0/1.4.2 across the lesson-4 and lesson-6 lockfiles) — ships secp256k1, P-256, Ed25519, X25519 and more; the elliptic-curve library behind Ethereum signing in modern JS toolchains. Quantum-vulnerable curve arithmetic rides along with every lesson build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the memory-hard KDF used by the ethereumjs stack for keystore/wallet files; transitive dep of the hardhat toolchain, no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js carries SHA-1 and SHA-2 implementations used by create-hash in the browserify cipher stack that hardhat ships; no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: elliptic@6.5.4 declared in lesson-4's lockfile (also 6.5.4/^6.5.2 entries inside other packages' dependency blocks) — classic JS elliptic-curve library (ECDSA/ECDH over secp256k1, P-256, etc.), pulled in transitively by the older Ethereum toolchain. Superseded upstream by @noble/curves, which is the migration path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: One logical asset with ALG-50e53f84: the hash.js library and the SHA family it provides. Lesson-4 builds with it transitively; no direct call site in application code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: pbkdf2@3.x (declared at lesson-4/package-lock.json:4646, "pbkdf2": "^3.0.17") — the Node PBKDF2 wrapper used by ethereumjs/ethers tooling for keystore-v3 wallet key derivation. Iteration count is fixed at runtime by the keystore format (ethers uses 262144 today), not by this manifest entry.
